gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-port-lligat-slab: Wide, wiry, and unmistakably technical. Nulshock is best at looking bold with a steady outline, while Port Lligat Slab, a text serif with porthole-wide counters, is best at hugging its letters into tidy lines.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-quando: A rope-thin outline, uniform all the way round, defines Nulshock. What stands out is the gap in temperament, since Quando, a serif with sparse spacing and tall middle zones, feels bookish beside that technical stretch.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-dm-sans: Oldtimer draws round, parenthesis-like forms with no swell on any downstroke. Beside it, DM Sans stays friendly, with wide-set terminals on the s, letting that commanding heading speak first.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Oldtimer's round forms curve like open parentheses, with no swell on any downstroke, for a firm, classic voice. Pilcrow Rounded, a sans with tight spacing and big counters, softens things with warmth and curves that refuse to close.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-fs-quicksand: No downstroke swells in Oldtimer, whose round forms bend like open parentheses and carry a classic, commanding look of their own. Oldtimer excels at command, Quicksand at gentle, glassy, bulb-round lowercase.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-aleo: Aleo, a serif whose counters let the eye slip in and out, carries a dignified, classic feel. But Oldtimer, free of hairlines and swells, leads with command, while Aleo is better at settling the eye.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-almendra-sc: Authoritative and dignified, the body face keeps its letter mouths open. Almendra SC, a serif, does the steady reading, while Oldtimer, with bowls matching its stems, does the commanding.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-antic-slab: Round forms that read like open parentheses make Oldtimer instantly commanding, with no swell on any downstroke. And Antic Slab, a text serif with round bowls, would sit comfortably a few sizes below it.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-arvo: Oldtimer has no hairlines at all, just round forms that bend like open parentheses. And Arvo, a serif with curves that refuse to close, backs the heading's command with traditional dignity.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-belgrano: Belgrano is classic and traditional, its open-mouthed curves staying clear. Under Oldtimer's round headings, which lack any pointed-brush swell, long reading in Belgrano would feel steady and unhurried.
